biography.plain_text: Keith Williams was an Australian tourism entrepreneur who created Sea World and developed Hamilton Island as a holiday destination. He built accommodation, a marina and a jet airport to attract visitors to the island. After losing control of that business, he developed Port Hinchinbrook, combining waterfront housing with tourism facilities.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before becoming a tourism developer, Keith Williams made leather motorcycle seats and accessories with help from his mother. He had left school to contribute to the household income, working at a petrol station and delivering telegrams. His manufacturing business expanded into licensed Disney products and water-ski equipment; he also became an Australian water-skiing champion.

His public responsibilities included serving as the first chairman of Gold Coast Tourism and chairing the Gold Coast Waterways Authority. Under his chairmanship, the authority began work on the Gold Coast Seaway. The project created a safer entrance between the ocean and the inland waterways used by commercial and recreational boats.
